title: Letters Of Light
paragraphs: “There doesn’t seem to be any particular danger.”

With that, Ren, Itsuki, and Father each stood in front of their respective monuments. Ren’s second row was glowing, Itsuki’s third row, and Father’s… his first row was glowing. No, rather, only Father’s… the Shield Hero’s section looked completely clear. There were no other inscriptions.
“What does it say?”
Ren began reading aloud.

“To the one who makes these letters shine: Your ability to analyze calmly and your sense of responsibility will become a source of strength. However, the time will come when your preconceived notions will bring you misfortune. Unless you distinguish between games and reality, you will not be able to avoid further tragedy. Accept reality, engage deeply with others, and broaden your perspective—that will be the key to saving the world. Even if you suffer defeat at the end of regret, relentless training will open the path to the future.”
It feels like this aligns somewhat with the Ren from the first world.
“It kind of overlaps with the failures Motoyasu-san told us about.”
“Yeah… though, after everything I’ve experienced this past month, this prophecy doesn’t seem all that useful right now…”
Ren stopped moving after reading the first row. Then, with a displeased expression, he furrowed his brows and stepped away.
“What’s wrong?”
“…No, don’t worry about it.”
“You recognized something?”
“Don’t read into it! It’s not about that guy!”
Itsuki and Father tilted their heads in confusion.
“So, I’m on the third row… I wonder what the criteria for this are.”
With that, Itsuki traced the letters with his finger.

“To the one who makes these letters shine: Your strong sense of justice will at times save a girl, and that girl will in turn save you. However, the time will surely come when you must question your own sense of justice. Your justice is merely a reflection of your own inferiority complex. As long as you fail to understand the true meaning of justice, the time when you can truly save others will never come. Continually question the path you believe in, and at the end of that struggle, the great decision you reach will elevate your justice to its true form.”
Itsuki also fell silent, lost in thought after reading the text.
“The text further below… it describes my traits. It mentions my high accuracy.”

Now that he mentioned it, there were still glowing sections further down. For me… it was something about an indomitable spirit that refuses to give up. There were other parts as well, but for some reason, they were distorted and unreadable.
“Ren.”
Father, looking concerned, reached out his hand, but Ren, still irritated, continued reading the lower section.
“Sense of responsibility, high concentration, analytical skills… and… mastery of trump cards… Hmph!”
Ren became even more agitated and completely averted his eyes from the monument.
What exactly was written there?
“Naofumi, what about you?”
Now that he mentioned it, Father’s monument was incredibly simple. All of its letters were glowing.

“Um… To the only one who makes these letters shine. No matter how much conspiracy torments you, as long as you do not lose your faith, the future remains open. Your true challenge is trust. Your unwavering heart, unbroken by adversity, will become the hope that dispels all darkness and forms an immutable future. And as long as there are those by your side whom you trust, you will become the will that protects the world from darkness. This is as far as I can see of the future. I pray that you will bring about the miracle that calms the waves…”
Compared to ours, this one feels a bit abstract, doesn’t it? That being said, the first line of each inscription seems similar to Father’s.
“Doesn’t Naofumi-san’s seem different? It doesn’t have the same paragraph breaks as the others.”
“And the writer even included their own personal wish.”
Ren and Itsuki were voicing their complaints.
“Well, I’ve decided not to believe in these inscriptions.”
Ren folded his arms and responded with clear irritation. I have no idea what he’s so dissatisfied about.
“So, was it the first row? What did it say?”
“Don’t try to figure it out. Shut up!”
“It was definitely a painful truth, huh… By the way, Ren-san, how do you master trump cards?”
“Shut up!”
Ren turned his face away, clearly refusing to talk about it.
“Naofumi-san, what about the lower part of the inscription?”
“Um… It mentions not getting drunk, being a behind-the-scenes supporter… speechcraft, negotiation. Are these the Shield Hero’s abilities?”
At that, Itsuki nodded. That makes sense. It really does feel like Father’s abilities.
“I see, that makes sense. That should be enough.”
“There’s still more, but it’s unreadable, so I guess that’s fine.”
“Still… this inscription is kind of irritating. The fact that it’s vaguely accurate makes it even worse.”
“Exactly!”
“What are the rest of them about?”
“They are said to be records of secret arts left behind for the heroes. Yes.”
The Pope explained.
“So it seems. There are magical symbols inscribed here that appear to be some kind of recipe. Is this alchemy?”

There are terms written here that seem like the specialized jargon Father used when he was studying alchemy in the first world. It’s likely that these inscriptions contain lost technologies. Perhaps, like the monument on Cal Mira Island, they also document special magic. If that’s the case… Considering that such monuments exist in both Faubrey and Cal Mira Island, it’s possible that similar ones are scattered all over the world.
“It can wait. Right now, getting to the castle takes priority.”
“You’re right. We should come back when we have more time and can properly read the magical inscriptions.”
“Hmm… This place seems like it could lead to many discoveries.”
Éclair, who had been silent until now, looked around the room and spoke.
“Judging by this, the Seven Star Heroes’ inscriptions are probably in the Seven Star Church.”

That might be the case. However, there are no Seven Star Hero companions here, and without the corresponding Seven Star Hero, I doubt we could read them. If we take the inscription on Cal Mira Island as an example, these inscriptions may only reveal their blessings to those who can actually read them.
“So dusty!”
“It’s a little hard to breathe.”
“Too dark!”
The filolials each shared their impressions.
“Alright, we’re heading to the castle now… Please take care of things here.”
“Yes. Heroes, I pray that you will save the world.”

The Pope smiled and guided us to the church’s exit. For now, he doesn’t seem like a bad person. …Then again, the Pope of a certain country also seemed like this at first. We left the Four Saints Church and headed toward the castle. A massive structure towered before us—the Faubrey Castle. No matter how many times I see it, it’s still enormous. As expected of the castle belonging to the world’s greatest nation.
“It’s really big.”
“Melromarc’s castle feels large too, but seeing this up close makes the difference clear.”
“Yeah. Even the castle gates are huge.”

As we arrived at the castle gates, we stepped down from the carriage and greeted the guards. It seemed they had been informed of our arrival, as they immediately saluted and opened the gates. The soldiers then guided us to park the carriage in the castle’s designated area. This is the first time Father and I have come here since we were caught in Takt’s trap. Though, I had visited once before in the first world.
“So… where do we go now? There’s a section over there that looks more like a town than part of the castle.”
“It seems we’re supposed to go this way.”

The soldiers welcomed us. For now, it doesn’t seem to have the same unpleasant feeling as during the incident with Takt. I’ve been to Faubrey Castle a few times before, so I remember some things about it. First, there’s the enormous castle itself, the centerpiece of the kingdom. It serves as the workplace for the king, knights, and various officials. Typically, when we have an audience, it happens here. The castle also has courtyards, and members of Faubrey’s royal bloodline with high ranks live within the castle itself. Those of lower rank reside in the town within the castle gates. The cost of living here is probably high, and security seems strict. With the soldiers guiding us, we were led into the castle. This place brings back memories. I recall the time Father was escorted to the Faubrey throne room, chatting with the Queen along the way. Oh, the soldiers at the castle’s reception desk are talking about something. One of them then turns to us with an apologetic look and bows.
“My apologies. His Majesty, the King of Faubrey, has not yet woken up and is still sleeping.”
…It’s already noon, though?
